H7_inode_headroom.reason: 225,490,340 free inodes against a +10y base projection of ~4.9M additional files -- roughly 46x headroom. Adjudication is the reviewer's, not this harness's.

h5_latency.cache_assumption: warm: one discarded request per window before sampling
h5_latency.finding: delta-only is the SLOWEST despite returning fewer days than base-only (41 vs 51). Delta is t1/s256 geometry -- one chunk per day -- so a 41-day delta read touches ~41 chunks per variable, while base's (90,8,8) chunking serves 51 days from far fewer. This is §10.1's claim that cadence, not block size, governs the read cost of the delta tail, measured on production for the first time.
h5_latency.label: VM24_PRODUCTION_READ_ONLY
h5_latency.method: 7 serial samples per window, 0.3 s apart, one warm request discarded first

candidates.operator_decision_required: EITHER verify base/hold value parity (var_valid and NaN semantics included) for the range, OR record an external recovery manifest with a usable download window, OR accept in writing that the local daily rebuild source is given up.
candidates.why_not_releasable: base covers the day SET gaplessly and the retention window has passed -- both necessary, neither sufficient. Base/hold VALUE parity was not verified, and no recovery source covers these days (local NetCDF starts 2026-07-12). Deleting them removes the only local rebuild source for 2023-01-01..2026-06-20.

candidates.basis: day sets read from each backup's own attributes; every day is covered by base (<=2026-06-26, gapless) or by the LIVE delta (2026-06-27..2026-08-17), which is the recovery source. Not on the serving path -- serving reads the live delta path, these sit under hold/. Not the rollback target: the 2026-08-18 backup is, and two later verified swaps supersede these. Expiry alone was treated as necessary, not sufficient.
candidates.caveat: value parity was not byte-verified; the basis is set coverage plus supersession

hold_lifecycle_audit.label: VM24_PRODUCTION_READ_ONLY
hold_lifecycle_audit.measurement_note: `du --block-size=1G` per directory summed to 2534 GiB against a 2347 GiB total, because it rounds each of 1267 entries UP. All figures here are `du -sb` bytes; the daily and backup totals sum to the measured hold total, which is the check that caught it.
hold_lifecycle_audit.method: hold/manifest.jsonl read + du -sb; no path was modified
hold_lifecycle_audit.p5_roots_note: p5_blocks / p5_repairs / p5_anchor / base_blocks are ABSENT, so there is no repair WAL to read. Repair state is therefore UNCHECKED, not clear. Round 1 reported these categories as 'empty', which read as a finding; the class is now `repair_state_unknown_pre_p5`.

recovery_sources.consequence: for the 1267 held daily days, the hold IS the only local rebuild source. Base can serve those days for point/range, but base is not a source you can rebuild base FROM.
recovery_sources.finding: the only local NetCDF holding is 32 files covering 2026-07-12..2026-08-17. It does NOT cover the daily hold range 2023-01-01..2026-06-20 -- not one day of it. There is no recorded external recovery manifest, download window or rebuild procedure on this host either.
recovery_sources.label: VM24_PRODUCTION_READ_ONLY
